params.body: {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.RestAttributeSensitivity}}: `sensitivityMode` code is required; an empty or missing list clears the non-sensitive attributes.

POST /rest/structure/2.0/attribute-sensi.summary: Checks whether a single attribute spec is acceptable for the sensitivity settings, without storing anything. Jira administrators only.

params.body: The JSON text of one {{com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.RestAttributeSpec}} (`id`, `format`, optional `params`).

POST /rest/structure/2.0/attribute-sensi.errors: 400 text/plain when the body is empty (`attribute spec is empty`-style message) or the spec cannot be parsed / has an unknown format (message gives the reason); 401 anonymous; 403 `permission violation` for non-administrators.

POST /rest/structure/2.0/attribute/subsc.summary: Creates an attribute-value subscription owned by the caller for a window (a forest, a set of its rows and a set of attributes) and optionally loads values right away. Subscriptions live in server memory on the node that created them, are private to their creator, expire after a period without use and are capped in number (10000 by default; oldest unused are dropped). Anonymous callers may subscribe. When clustered, the response sets a cookie `X-Structure-DC-Meta` = percent-encoded `<node id>|<retry count>` so the client can stick to the node.

params.valuesUpdate: When `true`, the reply includes `valuesUpdate` with attribute values; otherwise only the subscription id and window are returned.
params.valuesTimeout: Milliseconds to wait for value loading before answering (only with `valuesUpdate=true`). Default 1000 (configurable), clamped to 0..60000. Values not loaded in time are reported later with `stillLoading`.
params.body: {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.RestSubscriptionWindow}}: `forestSpec`, `rows` and `attributes` are all required for a new subscription.

POST /rest/structure/2.0/attribute/subsc.response: 200 with a {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.RestSubscriptionData}}: the new subscription id, the window as stored, and, with `valuesUpdate=true`, a full values update.
POST /rest/structure/2.0/attribute/subsc.errors: 400 when the forest spec is missing or invalid; attribute specs with unknown formats are silently dropped. 403 text/plain `permission violation` when the caller is not allowed to use Structure (plugin-wide user restriction); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

GET /rest/structure/2.0/attribute/subscr.summary: Returns the subscription's current window and, with `valuesUpdate=true`, the values that changed since the client's version. Also reports rows the caller cannot see and attribute loading errors collected since the last call.

params.skipLoading: When `true`, does not start or wait for value loading; reports only what is already loaded.
params.valuesUpdate: When `true`, the reply includes `valuesUpdate` with attribute values; otherwise only the subscription id and window are returned.
params.valuesTimeout: Milliseconds to wait for value loading before answering (only with `valuesUpdate=true`). Default 1000 (configurable), clamped to 0..60000. Values not loaded in time are reported later with `stillLoading`.
params.signature: Signature of the last values version the client holds (from `valuesUpdate.version`). Used with `version`; if either is missing the update is full (from version zero).
params.version: Version number the client holds, paired with `signature`; the update then only carries values that changed since that version.

POST /rest/structure/2.0/forest/update.summary: Applies a list of editing actions (add, copy, move, remove rows) to a forest in order, as the grid does on drag-and-drop, paste and delete. Each action may be accepted, refused with an error, or answered with a question (e.g. which generator should handle the change) that the client resolves by resending the remaining actions with the chosen value in the action's `parameters`. Processing stops at the first action that fails or asks a question. Effects in Jira caused by generators (field changes, links...) are reported for undo. A cut-and-paste between forests is an `add` with `cutFrom`: the removal from the source is first tried without changes, then the add is applied, then the removal; if the removal then fails, the add is undone where possible. When the cut went through the clipboard, the caller's clipboard is cleared after success. Usage counters are recorded. Runs as a server job: when the result is not ready within the asynchronous wait (3 s by default, configurable) the call answers 200 with only {{com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.RestJobId}} (`{"jobId": n}`) instead; the client repeats the call with that `jobId` in the body (other fields are then ignored) until the real response arrives. DELETE /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id.errors: 400 when the id is missing or not positive; 404 with a {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestStructureError}} when the structure is not viewable; 403 with a {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestStructureError}} when the caller can view but not administer it. Failures raised by Structure are answered with a {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestStructureError}} body and a status from the error category: 404 not found or not accessible, 403 no permission, 400 invalid input, 500 otherwise. Malformed JSON gives 400 with a {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestStructureError}} whose `error` is a parse-failure text; invalid request data gives 400 with `error` = `Invalid request data` and `message` = the reason; 503 (text) while Structure is stopped. 403 text/plain `permission violation` when the caller is not allowed to use Structure (plugin-wide user restriction); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/d.summary: Tells whether the structure is configured to show its description above the grid.
GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/d.errors: 403 text/plain when the structure does not exist or is not viewable. 403 text/plain `permission violation` when the caller is not allowed to use Structure (plugin-wide user restriction); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/f.summary: Tells whether the structure is one of the caller's favourites (always false for anonymous callers).
GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/f.errors: 403 text/plain when the structure does not exist or is not viewable. 403 text/plain `permission violation` when the caller is not allowed to use Structure (plugin-wide user restriction); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

PUT /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/f.summary: Adds the structure to, or removes it from, the caller's favourites. For anonymous callers nothing is stored and the answer is `false`.

params.body: {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.RestFavorite}} with the wanted state.

PUT /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/f.response: 200 with a {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.RestFavorite}}: the request echoed back (or `false` for anonymous).
PUT /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/f.errors: 403 text/plain when the structure does not exist or is not viewable. 403 text/plain `permission violation` when the caller is not allowed to use Structure (plugin-wide user restriction); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/q.summary: Returns the structure's configured quick transformations (the preset transformation buttons and groups shown above the grid).
GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/q.response: 200 with the stored JSON array of {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.RestTransformItem}} returned verbatim (`[]` when none).
GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/q.errors: 403 text/plain when the structure does not exist or is not viewable. 403 text/plain `permission violation` when the caller is not allowed to use Structure (plugin-wide user restriction); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

PUT /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/q.summary: Replaces the structure's quick transformations. Requires administer permission on the structure.

params.body: JSON array of {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.RestTransformItem}}; every item id, including ids of transformations inside groups, must be unique.

PUT /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/q.errors: 403 text/plain when the structure does not exist or the caller cannot administer it; 400 with a {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestStructureError}} when the body is missing, unparsable or has duplicate ids. 403 text/plain `permission violation` when the caller is not allowed to use Structure (plugin-wide user restriction); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

POST /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/.summary: Changes a structure's properties; properties absent from the body are kept. Requires administer permission. Setting `isArchived` to true on an active structure also disables its synchronizers. The owner can be changed (value `user:<key>` or a bare user key) only by Jira administrators, or by users with the user-picker permission who administer the structure or own it; an unknown user is ignored (logged).

params.body: {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.data.RestStructure}} with the properties to change.

POST /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/.response: 200 with the updated {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.data.RestStructure}} including permissions and owner.
POST /rest/structure/2.0/structure/{id}/.errors: 400 when the body is missing or invalid; 404 or 403 with a {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestStructureError}} when the structure is not visible or not administrable. Failures raised by Structure are answered with a {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestStructureError}} body and a status from the error category: 404 not found or not accessible, 403 no permission, 400 invalid input, 500 otherwise. Malformed JSON gives 400 with a {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestStructureError}} whose `error` is a parse-failure text; invalid request data gives 400 with `error` = `Invalid request data` and `message` = the reason; 503 (text) while Structure is stopped. 403 text/plain `permission violation` when the caller is not allowed to use Structure (plugin-wide user restriction); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

POST /rest/structure/2.0/synchronizers/u.summary: Undoes groups of actions previously performed by synchronizers (as recorded in the synchronizer audit log), processing the groups last to first. Only synchronizers that support undo do anything (the links synchronizer recreates or removes issue links; the agile synchronizer reverts epic and rank changes); for others a failure description is returned. The undo is performed as the caller and recorded in the synchronizer audit log. Logged-in users only; there is no structure or synchronizer permission check, and the undo operations use Jira's managers directly, so Jira permissions such as 'link issues' are not checked. Runs as a server job: when the result is not ready within the asynchronous wait (3 s by default, configurable) the call answers 200 with only {{com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.RestJobId}} (`{"jobId": n}`) instead; the client repeats the call with that `jobId` in the body (other fields are then ignored) until the real response arrives. An unknown or finished-and-collected `jobId` gives 404 with a {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestStructureError}} (code 4603); a `jobId` of another kind of job gives 400.

params.body: {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.RestSyncActions}}: `actionGroups[i]` is a JSON-array text of audit-log action objects and `syncModuleKeys[i]` the complete module key of the synchronizer that performed them (paired by index).

POST /rest/structure/2.0/synchronizers/u.response: 200 with a {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.RestSyncActions}}: `syncModuleKeys` echoed, `actionGroups` holding, for each input group in reverse order, the JSON-array text of the resulting undo actions or failure descriptions (`result`: `failure`, optional `reason`, optional `exception`).
POST /rest/structure/2.0/synchronizers/u.errors: 401 for anonymous callers. Failures raised by Structure are answered with a {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestStructureError}} body and a status from the error category: 404 not found or not accessible, 403 no permission, 400 invalid input, 500 otherwise. Malformed JSON gives 400 with a {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestStructureError}} whose `error` is a parse-failure text; invalid request data gives 400 with `error` = `Invalid request data` and `message` = the reason; 503 (text) while Structure is stopped. 403 text/plain `permission violation` when the caller is not allowed to use Structure (plugin-wide user restriction); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

POST /rest/structure/2.0/value.summary: Computes attribute values (column data) for given rows of one or more forests in one shot, without a subscription. Rows whose item no longer exists or is not visible to the caller get no values and are listed as inaccessible. Runs as a server job: when the result is not ready within the asynchronous wait (3 s by default, configurable) the call answers 200 with only {{com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.RestJobId}} (`{"jobId": n}`) instead; the client repeats the call with that `jobId` in the body (other fields are then ignored) until the real response arrives. An unknown or finished-and-collected `jobId` gives 404 with a {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestStructureError}} (code 4603); a `jobId` of another kind of job gives 400.

params.body: {{com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.RestValueRequest}}.

POST /rest/structure/2.0/value.request: `requests` is required; each entry needs a valid `forestSpec`; entries without rows or attributes produce an entry with only the spec. Attribute specs with unknown formats are dropped.
POST /rest/structure/2.0/value.response: 200 with a {{com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.RestValueResponse}} with one entry per request entry, in order.
POST /rest/structure/2.0/value.errors: 400 with a {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestStructureError}} when a forest spec is invalid. Failures raised by Structure are answered with a {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestStructureError}} body and a status from the error category: 404 not found or not accessible, 403 no permission, 400 invalid input, 500 otherwise. Malformed JSON gives 400 with a {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestStructureError}} whose `error` is a parse-failure text; invalid request data gives 400 with `error` = `Invalid request data` and `message` = the reason; 503 (text) while Structure is stopped. 403 text/plain `permission violation` when the caller is not allowed to use Structure (plugin-wide user restriction); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.name: effector-process-status
com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.summary: Life-cycle status of an effector process (a run of effectors that computes a preview of changes to Jira and then applies them).

values.CALCULATING: The preview of effects is being computed.
values.CALCULATED: Preview ready; waiting for the user to confirm.
values.QUEUED: Confirmed and waiting to be applied.
values.APPLY_INTERRUPTED: Application was interrupted (e.g. node shutdown); can be resumed.
values.APPLY_STOPPED: Application was cancelled by a user.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.Res.name: attribute-spec
com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.Res.summary: Identifies one attribute (a column value kind) together with the format in which its values are wanted. Two specs are equal when id, format and params are equal.

fields.id: Attribute id, e.g. `summary`, `key`, `status`, `duedate`, `created`, `item`, or an id understood by an installed attribute provider (formulas, aggregates, ...).
fields.params: Optional JSON object of attribute parameters (may nest other attribute specs, e.g. for totals); null/absent when none.
fields.format: Value format, one of `text`, `html`, `id`, `number`, `boolean`, `time` (milliseconds since the epoch), `duration` (milliseconds), `json` (object), `jsonArray`, `any`. Any other value is rejected (or the spec dropped where noted).

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.Res.name: forest-spec
com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.Res.summary: Names a forest the grid can display. Exactly one source must be given: a structure (`structureId`), a search query (`sQuery`), or the caller's clipboard (`type` = `clipboard`, private to the HTTP session); `transforms` then apply transformations on top.

fields.structureId: Structure id for a structure's forest.
fields.version: History version of the structure to show (read-only past state); only with `structureId`.
fields.sQuery: Search query whose results form the forest; see the query shape.
fields.type: `clipboard` for the caller's per-session clipboard forest; any other value is ignored.
fields.transforms: Ordered list of transformations (generators applied to the source as a view); null/absent = none.
fields.title: When `true`, the forest gets a title row for the structure on top; only with `structureId`.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.Res.name: forest-search-query
com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.Res.summary: A search whose results form a forest of up to 1000 items.

fields.query: Query text. Empty = show recently viewed issues (or recently viewed pages for `cql`).
fields.type: `jql` (Jira query), `text` (quick text search), `cql` (Confluence pages, requires the pages add-on), or a type contributed by an installed extension; otherwise the spec is rejected.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.Res.name: forest-transformation
com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.Res.summary: One transformation step applied to a forest view.

fields.module: Complete module key of the generator used as transformation (e.g. a sorter, filter or grouper).
fields.key: Client-side label of the step; ignored by the server and not part of equality.
fields.params: Generator parameters as a JSON object; null = defaults.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.Res.name: row-values-request
com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.Res.summary: One-shot request for attribute values of rows in one or more forests.

fields.jobId: Absent on the first call. Set to the `jobId` returned by an earlier call that timed out, to keep waiting for that job (see the endpoint).

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.Res.name: row-values-request-entry
com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.Res.summary: Rows and attributes wanted from one forest.

fields.forestSpec: The forest the rows belong to.
fields.rows: Row ids whose values are wanted; empty/absent = no values.
fields.attributes: Attributes wanted for every row; empty/absent = no values.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.Res.name: row-values-response
com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.Res.summary: Answer to a one-shot values request.

fields.responses: One entry per request entry, same order.
fields.itemTypes: Always an empty object in this answer.
fields.itemsVersion: The oldest items version on which the returned values are based (signature 0, version 0 when nothing was computed); a client can poll item changes from it.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.Res.name: row-values-attribute-column
com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.Res.summary: Values of one attribute for the answered rows.

fields.attribute: The attribute spec as normalized by the server (params null when empty).
fields.values: One value per row of the entry's `rows`, same order, encoded per the attribute's format; null when the row has no value.

fields.forestSpec: The spec from the request, echoed.
fields.rows: The rows actually answered, in request order, without inaccessible rows; absent when no rows or attributes were requested.
fields.data: One column per requested attribute (unknown-format attributes omitted).
fields.forestVersion: Version of the forest the values were computed against.
fields.inaccessibleRows: Requested rows whose item is missing or invisible to the caller; absent when none.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.Res.name: data-version
com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.Res.summary: A position in a server-side change stream (of a forest, of items, of a subscription's values). A client remembers the last version it received and asks for changes since it.

fields.signature: 32-bit number identifying the change stream instance; when the server's signature differs from the client's (e.g. after a restart or cache reset), versions are not comparable and the server sends a full update. 0 = no data yet.
fields.version: Counter within the stream, increasing with each change. With signature 0, version 0 means 'from scratch'.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.eff.name: applied-effect
com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.eff.summary: One change made outside the forest as a consequence of a grid action (e.g. a field updated or a link created by a generator).

fields.generatorRowId: Row id of the generator that caused it.
fields.external: True when the change was made in Jira data (outside Structure).
fields.reversible: True when it can be undone.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.eff.name: applied-effect-batch
com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.eff.summary: A group of effects applied together; the unit of undo/redo.

fields.batchId: Batch id, to be passed in `effectIds` of an undo/redo request.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.RestCop.name: structure-copy-progress
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.RestCop.summary: A running or recent structure-copy operation started from this structure.

fields.id: Background process id of the copy.
fields.status: `running` (queued or running), `waiting` (finished successfully, waiting to be acknowledged), or `failed`.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.RestMan.name: managed-structure-row
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.RestMan.summary: One row of the structure management table.

fields.name: Structure name.
fields.ownerKey: User key of the owner; null when none.
fields.myAccess: The caller's effective permission level on the structure.
fields.addons: Names of installed add-ons that integrate with this structure (only add-ons with a product icon), in a stable order.
fields.synchronizers: Installed synchronizers of the structure; empty when synchronization is not enabled.
fields.copyProcesses: Copy operations from this structure visible to the caller (only for logged-in callers).
fields.favorite: True when it is one of the caller's favourites.
fields.stars: Number of users who marked it favourite.
fields.lastOpened: Date the structure was last opened by anyone, formatted for the caller (date only); null when unknown.
fields.lastOpenedForSort: Same date as ISO-8601 `yyyy-MM-dd` for sorting; `0` when unknown.
fields.adjustable: True when manual adjustments are enabled for the structure.
fields.adjusted: True when manual adjustments exist (only computed when adjustable).
fields.problems: Set of problems to flag, see the problem shape; empty when none.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.RestMan.name: managed-structure-page-details
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.RestMan.summary: Extra per-structure data loaded only for the visible page of the management table.

fields.effectors: Number of effector rows in the structure (0 if it cannot be determined).
fields.descriptionHtml: Description rendered from Jira wiki markup to HTML (HTML-escaped text when no renderer).

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.RestMan.name: managed-structures-table
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.RestMan.summary: Rows of the structure management table plus the users they refer to.

fields.users: User details for the owners and the caller; callers who are neither Jira administrators nor allowed to pick users only receive their own entry (or none when anonymous).

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.RestSyn.name: managed-structure-synchronizer
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.RestSyn.summary: An installed synchronizer of a structure as shown in the management table.

fields.desc: Localized one-line description of the synchronizer and its configuration.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.name: forest-action
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.summary: One editing action in a forest update request.

fields.action: `add` (insert the sub-forest `forest`), `copy` (insert `forest` as copies of existing rows), `move` (move rows), `remove` (remove rows).
fields.rowId: Single row to move/remove (takes precedence over `rowIds`).
fields.forest: For `add`/`copy`: the rows to insert. Same row syntax as the forest encoding, but the `<item>` field is percent-decoded and then read as: a bare decimal = issue id; `<item type key>/<n>` or `<item type key>//<s>` with the full item type key (e.g. `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-folder/12`; the colon inside the key must be sent as `%3A`). New rows use negative temporary row ids; the server reports the ids it assigned.
fields.under: Parent row of the insert/move target; 0 or absent = top level.
fields.after: Sibling after which to place; 0 or absent = no such constraint (start of the parent).
fields.before: Sibling before which to place; 0 or absent = none.
fields.originalRowIds: For `copy`: for each row of `forest`, in order, the existing row it copies; length must equal the number of rows.
fields.cutFrom: For `add` (and `move` via clipboard): where the rows were cut from, so they are removed there.
fields.parameters: Answers to questions from a previous attempt (question parameter id → chosen value) and other action options; null = none.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.name: forest-action-cut-source
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.summary: The origin of rows being pasted after a cut.

fields.viaClipboard: True when the rows went through the caller's clipboard; the clipboard is cleared after success.
fields.spec: Forest the rows were cut from; when present, `version` and `rowIds` are required and the rows are removed there.
fields.version: Version of the source forest the row ids refer to.
fields.rowIds: Rows to remove from the source.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.name: attribute-sensitivity-settings
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.summary: Instance-wide policy for whether attribute values may reveal data from items the viewer cannot see.

fields.sensitivityMode: 0 = standard (attributes are sensitive except numbers, booleans, times, durations and the listed ones), 1 = strict (all attributes sensitive except the listed ones), 2 = permissive (no attribute is sensitive; the list is ignored).
fields.nonSensitiveAttributeSpecs: Attributes explicitly declared non-sensitive; sorted by id on output.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.name: automation-catalog
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.summary: Available automation modules and the caller's rights to configure them.

fields.generatorConfigurationAllowed: True when the caller holds the app permission to configure generators.
fields.effectorConfigurationAllowed: True when the caller holds the app permission to configure effectors.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.name: background-effector-process
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.summary: An effector process of the caller that is running or finished but not yet acknowledged, shown in the grid's background-process panel.

fields.linkUrl: Absolute URL `<base>/secure/StructureBoard.jspa[?s=<structure id>]#effectorProcessDialog=<process id>` opening the process dialog.
fields.finished: True when the status is completed, completed with errors, interrupted or stopped.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.name: create-item-request
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.summary: Request to create (or pick) an item and insert it as a row.

fields.jobId: Absent on the first call. Set to the `jobId` returned by an earlier call that timed out, to keep waiting for that job (see the endpoint).
fields.extensionRequests: Optional map from core-extension key to an extension-specific request; each installed extension may answer under the same key in `extensionData`.
fields.forest: Forest to insert into and the client's version of it (required).
fields.items: The client's items version (required); the response reports item changes since it.
fields.rowId: Temporary row id the client assigned to the new row (negative); reported back in `oldRowIds`.
fields.item: The item: an existing `itemId`, or `type` and `values` for a new item.
fields.semantics: Row semantics number for the new row; 0/absent = none.
fields.parameters: Answers to earlier questions, e.g. `{"0:CreateAnyway": true}`; null = none.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.name: create-item-response
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.summary: Result of creating and inserting an item.

fields.successfulActions: 1 when the row was inserted (or an existing generated row was used), otherwise 0.
fields.updateError: Present when an action was refused or a question must be answered; absent on success.
fields.forestUpdates: Forest changes since the client's version(s), so the client can resynchronize.
fields.itemTypes: Map from the decimal item-type numbers used in this response's forest or item encodings to full item type keys (e.g. `"3": "com.almworks.jira.structure:type-folder"`). Only types that occur in this response are listed.
fields.oldRowIds: The client's temporary row id (and other replaced ids), parallel to `newRowIds`.
fields.newRowIds: The real row id of the inserted row (and other replacements).
fields.effects: Effect batches applied in Jira by this request.
fields.problems: Effects that could not be applied.
fields.extensionData: Map from core-extension key to extension-specific data returned for the request's `extensionRequests`; absent or null when no extension answered.
fields.formErrors: Item validation messages not tied to a field; absent when none.
fields.fieldErrors: Item validation messages by field id; absent when none.
fields.itemId: Full id of the created or inserted item (`<item type key>/<n>`, `<item type key>//<s>`, or bare issue id); absent when nothing was created.
fields.itemsUpdate: Item changes since the client's items version.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.name: structure-description-shown-flag
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.summary: Whether the structure's description is shown above the grid.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.name: effect-problem
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.summary: An effect that a generator wanted to apply but could not.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.name: effect-record
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.summary: One effect of an effector process: in a preview, a change that would be made; in the audit records, a change that was made.

fields.affectedItems: Items the effect touches, with display text and URL.
fields.undo: HTML-escaped description of the reverting change (applied records only; absent for errors).
fields.effect: Description of the change as HTML (escaped text, or provider-supplied HTML).
fields.isError: True when the effect failed or cannot be applied (e.g. its provider is not installed); absent otherwise.
fields.timestamp: When it was applied, milliseconds since the epoch (0 in previews).
fields.index: Position of the effect in the process's preview.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.name: effector-module-info
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.summary: An available effector module.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.name: effector-process
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.summary: An effector process as listed in the audit view.

fields.userKey: Key of the user who started it.
fields.user: Details of that user; null when the user no longer exists.
fields.started: Start time formatted for the caller (complete date-time style); empty string when unknown.
fields.finished: Finish time formatted the same way; empty when not finished.
fields.structure: Structure the process ran on; null for one-off runs without a structure.
fields.effectors: Effectors that ran (or, for a one-off run, a single entry with only a name).
fields.revertedProcessId: For an undo process, the process it reverts; null otherwise.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.name: effector-process-effector
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.summary: An effector that took part in a process.

fields.id: Effector instance id; null for one-off runs.
fields.name: Display name with configuration summary.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.name: effector-process-structure
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.summary: The structure of an effector process.

fields.name: Structure name; null when the caller can no longer view it.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.name: effector-process-progress
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.summary: Status and progress of an effector process.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.name: forest-action-error
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.summary: Why an action was refused.

fields.row: Row the error is about; 0 when none.
fields.itemDescription: Display text of that row's item (or `row <id>` when unknown).
fields.itemUrl: URL of that item; null when none.
fields.itemCount: Number of rows the failed action involved.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.name: structure-favorite-flag
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.summary: Favourite state of a structure for the caller.

com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.name: structure-history-page
com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v2.data.summary: A list of structure history versions.

fields.versions: Versions, newest first; absent when there are none.

fields.version: The new version; the client stores it. Absent when the forest could not be read.
fields.formula: Present for a full update (client must replace its forest). Forest encoding: rows in depth-first order separated by `,`; each row is `<rowId>:<depth>:<item>`, followed by `:<semantics>` only when the row's semantics number is positive. Empty string = empty forest.
fields.updates: Present for an incremental update: changes separated by `|`, applied in order. `a.<under>.<after>.<forest>` inserts the encoded sub-forest under row `under` (0 = top level) after sibling `after` (0 = first position), depths relative to the insertion point; `m.<under>.<after>.<rows>` moves the comma-separated rows (with their sub-trees) there; `r.<rows>` removes the comma-separated rows; `o.<under>.<rows>` reorders the children of `under` into the given order.
